
## Why This Is Asked

- Circuit breakers, timeouts, exponential backoff

## Code Example

```javascript
// Pseudo-code sketch of a simple circuit breaker
class CircuitBreaker {
  constructor(threshold, timeout) { this.state='CLOSED'; this.failures=0; this.lastAttempt=0; this.threshold=threshold; this.timeout=timeout; }
  call(fn) { if (this.state==='OPEN') throw new Error('Breaker open'); try { const res=fn(); if (res) this.failures=0; else this.failures++; if (this.failures>this.threshold) this.state='OPEN'; return res; } catch(e){ this.failures++; if (this.failures>this.threshold) this.state='OPEN'; throw e; } }
}
```

- What telemetry would prove the strategy preserves UX during degradation?

## Interview Context
This question assesses SRE expertise in incident management, automation, and process improvement - critical skills for maintaining system reliability.

## Technical Implementation
- **Incident Response**: PagerDuty/VictorOps integration with automated escalation policies based on severity levels
- **Root Cause Analysis**: Distributed tracing with Jaeger/Tempo to correlate microservice calls across the infrastructure
- **Timeline Generation**: Automated collection of logs, metrics, and traces into structured timeline visualizations
- **Postmortem Automation**: Python/Node.js service using GPT-4 to generate draft postmortems from incident data

## NFRs & Calculations
- **Availability**: 99.9% uptime for postmortem system (8.76 hours downtime/month max)
